the processing of corn did not affect performance when the diets contained 60% WCGF and 14% CP.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
corn processing and protein concentration in the finishing ration did not influence performance of steers fed wet corn gluten feed.
corn processing method and protein supplementation did not have a significant effect on feed intake and performance when WCGF was included in the finishing diet.
the use of wet corn gluten feed as an alternative protein source in finishing diets is feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corn processing method and protein concentration in finishing diets containing wet corn-gluten feed have minimal effects on cattle performance and carcass characteristics.
corn processing method has a significant effect on feedlot performance and carcass merit of cattle fed diets containing wet corn distillers grains.
the processing method of the corn in the feedlot diet does not affect performance, carcass characteristics or the ability of the cattle to utilize the wet corn gluten feed in the diet.
